cosmic rays can drive the formation of complex interstellar organic molecules in cold interstellar clouds.
cosmic ray-driven radiation-chemical processes are likely to be important under cold core conditions, and that these processes can lead to the enhanced formation of complex organic compounds.
cosmic rays can drive chemical reactions in the solid phase and that these reactions can lead to the enhanced formation of complex organic species.

understanding the chemical effects of ionizing cosmic rays on interstellar ices and the gas phase.
the effect of cosmic ray-driven grain chemistry on the formation and abundance of complex organic molecules in cold dense interstellar clouds.

cosmic rays can be an effective source of complex organic molecules under cold core conditions, and that the chemistry is likely to be important for the chemistry of interstellar ice mantles, but not necessarily for gas-phase chemistry.
radiation-chemistry is a viable and important formation mechanism for many complex organic molecules, and that it should be taken into consideration in astrochemical models.
cosmic rays can have a significant effect on solid-phase and gas-phase chemistry in cold interstellar clouds, and this effect is not yet fully understood.

the inclusion of non-thermal chemistry in astrochemical models is essential for the accurate modeling of the chemical composition and evolution of the ISM.
the inclusion of cosmic rays can lead to a significant enhancement of complex organic molecules in both gas and ice mantles in dense interstellar environments.
cosmic-ray-driven chemistry is an additional, important mechanism for the formation of complex molecules in cold interstellar clouds.
The main takeaway from our work is that

cosmic-ray-induced chemistry in the ice mantles and gas phases of cold interstellar clouds is an important chemical mechanism that should be taken into account when modeling the chemistry of these environments.
radiation chemistry is a potentially important source of organic molecules in interstellar ices and gas, particularly in environments that may be exposed to high ionization rates.
cosmic rays are a potentially important driver of interstellar chemistry, and should be taken into account in future models.
